title: Kirby Problem 2.24
statement:
Does there exist a complex surface $X$ that admits three or more
non-isomorphic structures as a surface bundle over a surface?
background:
Source: Kirby's Problems in Low-Dimensional Topology notes. Original problem number: KP-2.24.

Literature notes:
(1) The analogous situation in the case of surface bundles over the circle is
organized by the Thurston norm [Thu86]: if a surface bundle over the
circle admits two different fibrations, then it admits infinitely many. By
contrast, work of F.E.A. Johnson [Joh99] shows that a given 4-manifold
admits only finitely many structures as a surface bundle over a surface
with base and fiber both of genus $\geq 2$.
(2) Atiyah [Ati69] and Kodaira [Kod67] constructed complex surfaces $X$
that are surface bundles over surfaces in two distinct ways. These are
constructed as branched covers of products of algebraic curves; the two
bundle structures arise from the projections onto either factor. Certain
families of these examples admit exactly two fiberings by work of Chen
[Che18], Salter–Tshishiku [ST20], and Landesman–Litt–Sawin [LLS25].
The problem formulated here was also raised by Catanese [Cat17].
(3) In the smooth category, Salter [Sal15] gave a method of constructing
surface bundles over surfaces (with base and fiber each of genus at least
2) with an arbitrary finite number of fiberings. However, these are known
not to admit complex structures.

References cited:
- [Thu86] William P. Thurston. A norm for the homology of 3-manifolds. Mem. Amer. Math. Soc., 59(339):i–vi and 99–130, 1986.
- [Joh99] F. E. A. Johnson. A rigidity theorem for group extensions. Arch. Math. (Basel), 73(2):81–89, 1999. doi:10.1007/s000130050371.
- [Ati69] M. F. Atiyah. The signature of fibre-bundles. In Global Analysis (Papers in Honor of K. Kodaira), pages 73–84. Univ. Tokyo Press, Tokyo, 1969.
- [Kod67] K. Kodaira. A certain type of irregular algebraic surfaces. J. Analyse Math., 19:207– 215, 1967. doi:10.1007/BF02788717.
- [Che18] Lei Chen. The number of fiberings of a surface bundle over a surface. Algebr. Geom. Topol., 18(4):2245–2263, 2018. doi:10.2140/agt.2018.18.2245.
- [ST20] Nick Salter and Bena Tshishiku. Arithmeticity of the monodromy of some Kodaira fibrations. Compos. Math., 156(1):114–157, 2020. doi:10.1112/s0010437x19007668.
- [LLS25] Aaron Landesman, Daniel Litt, and Will Sawin. Big monodromy for higher Prym representations. Geom. Topol., 29(5):2733–2782, 2025. doi:10.2140/gt.2025.29.2733.
- [Cat17] Fabrizio Catanese. Kodaira fibrations and beyond: methods for moduli theory. Jpn. J. Math., 12(2):91–174, 2017. doi:10.1007/s11537-017-1569-x.
- [Sal15] Nick Salter. Surface bundles over surfaces with arbitrarily many fiberings. Geom. Topol., 19(5):2901–2923, 2015. doi:10.2140/gt.2015.19.2901.

## Literature review (checked 2026-08-17)

**Status:** partially_solved  
**Classification:** PARTIAL-PROGRESS

**Current literature assessment.** Complex surfaces with two bundle structures are known, and smooth examples have arbitrarily many, but no complex surface with three or more nonisomorphic surface-bundle structures was verified.

**Verified partial progress.**

- Atiyah and Kodaira give complex two-fibration examples.
- Several families are proved to have exactly two.
- Salter constructs smooth examples with any prescribed finite number.

**Full solution or refutation.**

The complex-category three-fibration question remains open.

**What remains.**

Construct or rule out a complex example with at least three fibreings.

**Sources checked.**

- K3: A New Problem List in Low-Dimensional Topology, Problem 2.24 (2026). (authoritative_secondary): https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/kirbylistrep.pdf
  Evidence used: Distinguishes complex two-fibration results from smooth arbitrarily-many examples.

**Review notes.** No source alteration.

This is a dated literature triage; an open classification is not proof that no later or unindexed result exists.
